summary.name: Shrinking the time to mitigate production incidents
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud blog post by the CRE team on training incident responders to reduce time to mitigate outages, using DiRT disaster recovery tests and Wheel of Misfortune role-playing exercises.
use_cases: Training on-call engineers to respond to production outages
Running a simulated incident role-play with a team
Planning disaster recovery tests in a company
Reducing time to mitigate service incidents
summary.what_it_does: The article explains why untrained incident responders slow mitigation, even when incident management is in place. It describes Google's DiRT (Disaster Recovery Testing) approach, which coordinates real and fictitious outages under rules of engagement, requires rollback plans, and gets test review and approval. It describes the Wheel of Misfortune, a role-playing exercise where a Dungeon Master runs a simulated emergency that responders debug without affecting production. It advises starting with small service-specific tests and links to test plan and Wheel of Misfortune templates.
notable: Describes Google's DiRT disaster recovery testing rules of engagement and approval process
Wheel of Misfortune role-playing format run by a Dungeon Master, with no production impact
Links to downloadable Test Plan Scenario and Wheel of Misfortune templates
caveats: DiRT exercises operate on production services and can cause user-facing outages or revenue loss
Recommends starting small; large DiRT tests need cross-functional review and possibly VP-level approval for high-risk tests
